Simple Present usage: to express universal truths, facts, customs; habitual, routine actions; a permanent state; in exclamatory sentences; in subordinate clauses beginning with if and when in imperative sentences; to indicate a planned future action related to a journey; in running commentaries; to introduce quotations; with verbs like to love, to hate, to think.

Verbs of perception and some other verbs are not generally used in the present continuous tense, for example see, smell, hear, taste, know, understand, hate, like, want, wish, etc.
